name: Built to Spill
label: Up Records
lede: A Boise guitarist tried to never have a hit, kept a rotating cast, and ended up with three records on Pitchfork's list of the 1990s.

eras.title: A Boise kid in a Seattle van
eras.text: Doug Martsch is 19 when he joins Treepeople, a Boise band that moves to Seattle and plays punk bills instead of grunge ones. Three years in, he wants his own thing.

years.src: Wikipedia: Treepeople · Seattle Weekly: Spilled history · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill
years.h: [[Treepeople|dec1aede-420e-4381-bfb7-e87ba02f25d6]] start in Boise with Doug Martsch on guitar
years.p: Pat Brown, Wayne Flower and Scott Schmaljohn, all ex-State of Confusion, add Martsch as the fourth member.
years.xp:
The band ends up in Seattle on C/Z Records, but Seattle Weekly notes it never sat in the Sub Pop grunge scene; Treepeople played all-ages bills with punk and straight-edge bands instead.

Their sound sat, in one critic's words, between late-80s Hüsker Dü and the first Sugar album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Treepeople · Seattle Weekly: Spilled history
years.h: Wayne Flower leaves Treepeople; Pat Brown follows before album three
years.p: Martsch is now the songwriter in a band losing its founders.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates Flower's exit to 1991 and Brown's to before the third album, Just Kidding (1993). Flower resurfaces in the [[The Halo Benders|859c297a-f739-45f2-ac58-401eeb2d017f]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill · MusicianGuide: Built to Spill Biography
years.h: Martsch quits Seattle and starts Built to Spill in Boise
years.p: The name came from an exquisite-corpse-style word game he played with his wife. The plan: he stays, everyone else rotates.
years.xp:
Martsch's original idea was to be the only permanent member and pick new backing musicians for each album. He left [[Treepeople|dec1aede-420e-4381-bfb7-e87ba02f25d6]] in 1992 (Encyclopedia.com and MusicianGuide say so; Wikipedia says the group ended in 1994).

That rotating-cast idea got dropped for about two decades, then came back. See 2018.

eras.title: Wavers, Halo Benders, and a record about growing up
eras.text: A trio debut on C/Z, a side project with the man who ran K Records, then the record most people meet first. Up Records, a new Seattle label, puts it out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill
years.h: Ultimate Alternative Wavers: debut on C/Z, trio lineup
years.p: [[Doug Martsch|42c520b5-4992-4aab-9f3f-542addcde686]] plays with guitarist [[Brett Netson|7f1c14ad-ac89-46d7-9583-64dfb46f4fa7]] of Caustic Resin and drummer [[Ralf Youtz|0fad8c79-2420-4758-b41e-207ba8dc136b]]. Neil Young and Dinosaur Jr. are all over it.
years.xp: One guide dates the album to 1991; Wikipedia, MusicianGuide and Encyclopedia.com say 1993. Netson and Youtz were gone by the next record, replaced by Brett Nelson and Andy Capps.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Halo Benders · MONSTERFRESH: Unearthed Built To Spill / Halo Benders Concert From 1994
years.h: [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] and Martsch start the Halo Benders
years.p: The K Records founder and the Boise guitarist trade verses and write separate songs. Their first LP is God Don't Make No Junk.
years.xp:
Ralf Youtz, Wayne Flower and later Steve Fisk fill out the band. Unearthed video8 footage from the Capitol Theater in Olympia shows Built to Spill playing the still-unreleased There's Nothing Wrong with Love and then the Halo Benders taking the stage, though the exact date is not settled.

Wikipedia also records that the band got pulled over in Utah in the 1990s while a crew was filming Real Stories of the Highway Patrol. They reformed for Boise shows in 2007 and a 2010 Olympia benefit.

years.src: Wikipedia: Up Records
years.h: Up Records opens in Seattle with Built to Spill on the roster
years.p: Chris Takino and Rich Jensen found the label in 1994; it would put out over 100 releases.
years.xp:
Takino died of leukemia in 2000 and Pete Ritchey took over running the label. Its website stopped updating in 2007 and it wound down in 2008; around 2018 its assets were licensed to Sub Pop, which now releases Built to Spill.

Modest Mouse, Duster, 764-HERO, Quasi and Tad were also on the roster.

years.src: Wikipedia: There's Nothing Wrong with Love · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill
years.h: There's Nothing Wrong with Love: Brett Nelson's first record
years.p: Recorded May to June at John & Stu's in Seattle with Phil Ek. Andy Capps plays drums on this album and no other.
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls it a concept album about growing up. "Reasons" was written for Karena Youtz, then Martsch's wife, and "Cleo" is sung from the point of view of their unborn child; Encyclopedia.com says the song is about his son.

Singles were "Car" and "Distopian Dream Girl". Pitchfork gave it 9.3 and later ranked it 24th on its 1990s list. Sub Pop reissued it on vinyl in 2015.

eras.title: Lollapalooza and a Warner deal
eras.text: A rarities album, a benefit track, a summer tour and a three-album contract with Warner Bros. all land in the same stretch.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · MusicianGuide: Built to Spill Biography
years.h: Built to Spill Caustic Resin: a split EP with Brett Netson's band
years.p: Also this year: the track "Still Flat" for the AIDS benefit compilation Red Hot + Bothered.
years.xp: Caustic Resin is [[Brett Netson|7f1c14ad-ac89-46d7-9583-64dfb46f4fa7]]'s band, from Boise. Netson would return to Built to Spill's lineup in the 2000s and play on You in Reverse.

years.big: Health insurance for a newborn was part of the reason
years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · Wikipedia: Perfect from Now On · Consequence: Interview: Doug Martsch · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill
years.h: Warner Bros. signs a band that would rather not have a hit
years.p: Martsch says he wrote long songs so radio would ignore him: "I didn't want us to have a hit."
years.xp:
The deal, per Wikipedia, was three albums with real creative control. Martsch has credited the band's lawyer, who had worked with R.E.M., Sonic Youth and Dinosaur Jr., and said: "I don't know why they let us do what we do, but they have."

Wikipedia reports the health-insurance motive, tied to Martsch's newborn son. Scott Plouf, a former Spinanes drummer, is the drummer by now.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lync · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill
years.h: The Normal Years collects the singles and odd tracks
years.p: Lollapalooza and a European run supporting the Foo Fighters come around this time.
years.xp: Wikipedia's [[Lync|65e1b41c-c719-4237-9f72-c2f07ea19355]] entry says the Olympia band's bassist James Bertram and drummer Dave Schneider joined Built to Spill as touring musicians, as documented on this release. Sources differ on whether the Lollapalooza dates were 1995 or 1996.

eras.title: Three long songs, then a short-song record
eras.text: Perfect from Now On is the anti-hit. Its follow-up, with Brett Nelson and Scott Plouf writing alongside Martsch, is the closest they come to one.

years.src: Wikipedia: Perfect from Now On
years.h: A hot car ruins the first take of Perfect from Now On
years.p: Master tapes were damaged by heat on producer Phil Ek's drive from Seattle to Boise. The failed attempts cost $20,000.
years.xp: Wikipedia's account has three sessions. Martsch first played nearly everything but drums himself; he and Ek both hated it. The second attempt, with Nelson and Plouf, was the one that got cooked. [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] encouraged them to try again.

years.src: Wikipedia: Perfect from Now On · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill · Consequence: Interview: Doug Martsch
years.h: Perfect from Now On: seven of eight songs top six minutes
years.p: Warner Bros. debut, finished at Avast! in Seattle. Pitchfork ranks it 22nd on its 1990s list.
years.xp:
By February 1999 it had sold 43,000 copies, according to Wikipedia. Encyclopedia.com puts it at about 40,000.

Martsch later told Consequence the band grew out of the rotating-cast plan around this record because he wanted "more collaborative music".

years.src: Wikipedia: The Halo Benders · Consequence: Interview: Doug Martsch
years.h: Halo Benders release The Rebels Not In
years.p: Their third and last K Records album; the band's earlier ones were God Don't Make No Junk (1994) and Don't Tell Me Now (1996).
years.xp: Martsch told Consequence that Halo Benders attempts at new material later sent some songs to Built to Spill.

years.big: Warner cleared it at the last minute
years.src: Wikipedia: Keep It Like a Secret
years.h: "You Were Right" strings together a classic-rock jukebox
years.p: Martsch built the song from lines of the Rolling Stones, the Doors, Jimi Hendrix, Bob Dylan and others.
years.xp: Martsch explained the method: "I decided to use other people's clichés." Wikipedia says Warner secured the copyright clearances late.

years.src: Wikipedia: Keep It Like a Secret · Wikipedia: Built to Spill · MusicianGuide: Built to Spill Biography
years.h: Keep It Like a Secret: shorter songs, first Billboard 200 entry
years.p: It debuts at No. 120 and sells 60,000 copies in its first year, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
Martsch said he was burned out on long songs. The band held week-long jam sessions in Boise with him triggering a tape deck by foot pedal, then he mined the tapes. Tracking began in November 1997 at Bear Creek in Woodinville, with overdubs at Avast! in mid-1998.

Pitchfork gave it 9.3 and named it 1999's best album. Karena Youtz contributed lyrics, according to MusicianGuide.

years.src: Wikipedia: Treepeople · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill
years.h: Pat Brown, the Treepeople bassist, dies
years.p: Wikipedia says he died by suicide in 1999; one guide places it two months after Keep It Like a Secret.
years.xp: Martsch would dedicate the 2006 album You in Reverse to Brown.

eras.title: Live, solo, and back to short songs
eras.text: A live double, a return to three-minute songs, and Martsch alone with a blues record.

years.src: Seattle Weekly: Spilled history · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill
years.h: Ancient Melodies of the Future: 40 minutes, no long ones
years.p: A deliberate return to the shorter pop songs of There's Nothing Wrong with Love, after the live album Live (2000).
years.xp: Bearded Gentlemen's guide calls "Strange" the band's best pop song.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · MusicianGuide: Built to Spill Biography
years.h: Martsch goes solo with Now You Know
years.p: Blues and folk, with Delta blues the reference point in one bio.
years.xp: Built to Spill went quiet while it came out; from 2003 to 2005 the band toured 150-plus dates.

eras.title: Four guitars, a bad eye, and a funeral
eras.text: You in Reverse finally comes out after two years on a shelf. That spring, Martsch's retina detaches and Andy Capps is found dead.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · Consequence: Interview: Doug Martsch · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill
years.h: You in Reverse: recorded in 2004, released two years later
years.p: Made in Portland with four guitarists, including [[Jim Roth|cc7cb41f-c7c3-4ad3-916e-bf139a9c7ab4]] and [[Brett Netson|7f1c14ad-ac89-46d7-9583-64dfb46f4fa7]]. Dedicated to Pat Brown.
years.xp:
Martsch told Consequence that he and engineer Steve Lobdell made it at Audible Alchemy in Portland. It was less collaborative than he wanted, with less jamming time.

One reviewer describes it as a "Television album": long interlocking guitars, back to extended songs.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill
years.h: Touring resumes after Andy Capps dies; "Car" is dedicated to him
years.p: Capps was found dead in his Idaho home on May 18. Martsch also had retina surgery in March, which cancelled South by Southwest.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band dedicated performances of "Car" to Capps. He had played drums only on There's Nothing Wrong with Love.

years.h: There Is No Enemy gets Bob Odenkirk to direct a video
years.p: Its "Hindsight" clip comes a year later; Wikipedia calls the album the band's highest-charting.

eras.title: New rhythm section, old Warner
eras.text: After 18 years Nelson and Plouf are out, and Martsch, Jason Albertini and Stephen Gere make the last Warner album as a trio.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: A secret Portland show debuts a new rhythm section
years.p: Jason Albertini (Helvetia, Duster) on bass and Stephen Gere on drums play Bunk Bar by invitation. Nelson and Plouf's exit is announced January 7, 2013.
years.xp: Martsch later said an album made in 2012 was abandoned because of the departures and his own dissatisfaction.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: Untethered Moon: a trio record with Sam Coomes co-producing
years.p: Martsch, Albertini and Gere record it, and Coomes of Quasi, a frequent touring keyboardist, co-produces.
years.xp: Netson and Jim Roth left in the second half of 2015; a three-piece debuted in spring 2016.

years.h: Built to Spill and Warner Bros. part after 22 years
years.p: The split is announced with no new label named.

eras.title: Back to the rotating cast
eras.text: Martsch says out loud that the band is going back to his first idea. It is a Sub Pop band now, and the Treepeople get back together.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: Martsch announces a rotating cast for each record, again
years.p: Brazilian musicians João Casaes and Lê Almeida become the rhythm section for South American dates.
years.xp: Martsch posted it on Facebook. By 2019, Melanie Radford was on bass and Teresa Esguerra on drums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Treepeople
years.h: Treepeople reunite with Troy Wright on bass
years.p: The original lineup returns in 2018 with Wright replacing Pat Brown; the reunion ends with a final tour in August 2023.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the final tour covered the Pacific Northwest and Idaho.

years.h: A whole album of Daniel Johnston covers
years.p: Built to Spill play his songs; it is a cover album, not new material.

years.h: Built to Spill sign to Sub Pop
years.p: The label that reissued There's Nothing Wrong with Love on vinyl in 2015 becomes their home.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: When the Wind Forgets Your Name: first new songs since 2015
years.p: Recorded before COVID with the Brazilian rhythm section, Casaes and Almeida.
years.xp: Sub Pop released it; the album is the band's first since Untethered Moon.

years.h: 30 years of There's Nothing Wrong with Love, played front to back
years.p: The anniversary tour starts in August with Yo La Tengo.
